facts.t: The Constitution never defines an office of profit
facts.d: Articles 102(1)(a) and 191(1)(a) disqualify a person for holding one — without saying what it is. Every element of the concept has been built by courts, case by case, over seventy years.

facts.t: Twenty MLAs lost their seats over one post
facts.d: In 2018 the President, acting on the Election Commission's recommendation, disqualified twenty Delhi MLAs appointed as Parliamentary Secretaries. Around twenty states have created such posts, and courts have struck down several of those appointments.

facts.t: Profit is required, but regularity is not
facts.d: Prestige alone is not enough — Hedge v. Karnataka insists on pecuniary advantage. But Hotilal v. Bahadur held the income need not be regular, so an occasional or one-off payment can still bring the office within the bar.

bank.q: With reference to the three essentials in S. Umrao Singh, consider the following:
s: The person must hold an office.
The office must be one of profit.
The office must be under the Government.
bank.e: All three must be satisfied cumulatively — failure on any one takes the case outside Articles 102(1)(a) and 191(1)(a).

bank.q: Which case established that mere prestige is insufficient and pecuniary advantage is necessary?
o: S. Umrao Singh v. Darbara Singh
bank.e: Hedge v. Karnataka (1993). Hotilal held separately that the income need not be regular.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (principle):
pairs: 1. The holder must be legally capable of holding the office
B. Ghulam Chand v. Thakur Singh
2. Government control over the office is pivotal
bank.e: Hotilal on irregular income, Ghulam Chand on legal capacity, Ashok Kumar Bhattacharya on control, and Guru Govinda Basu on the power of appointment and removal.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the four tests in Swapan Roy v. Pradyut Bordoloi?
o: Government control over the office's functions
Whether the office existed before the Constitution
bank.e: The fourth test is conflict of interest, described as the crucial factor.

bank.as: The office of profit bar rests on separation of powers.
bank.rs: It prevents a conflict between duty and interest in a person who is both legislator and part of the executive.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the same rationale that led the Second ARC to focus on executive decision-making power rather than remuneration alone.

bank.q: With reference to the Second ARC's recommendations, consider the following:
s: Purely advisory bodies should not count as offices of profit, regardless of remuneration.
Executive decision-making power combined with control over public funds should count.
Offices requiring close coordination with the Council of Ministers should always be treated as offices of profit.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The ARC took the opposite view on the third — such offices, being essential to government functioning, should not attract the bar.

bank.q: The 2018 disqualification of Delhi MLAs was ordered by:
o: The Speaker of the Delhi Assembly
The President, on the Election Commission's recommendation
bank.e: The President acting on the ECI's recommendation, which is the constitutional route for office-of-profit disqualification.

bank.q: All of the following are relevant to determining an office of profit EXCEPT:
o: The extent of government control over the office
Whether remuneration is paid by the government
The prestige attached to the office
The presence of a conflict of interest
bank.e: Prestige alone is expressly insufficient — Hedge v. Karnataka requires pecuniary advantage.

bank.q: Who observed that a practical view, rather than a pedantic basket of tests, should guide the inquiry?
bank.e: Prof. P. D. T. Achary, in Practice and Procedure of Parliament — a caution against mechanical application of the judicial tests.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the legal position:
s: The Constitution defines an office of profit exhaustively.
Parliamentary Secretary posts have been created in around twenty states.
Courts have struck down several such appointments.
bank.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. There is no statutory or constitutional definition — the entire concept is judge-made.
